title: Stickler Syndrome: The Master Guide
summary: Stickler Syndrome (Hereditary Progressive Arthro-ophthalmopathy) is a multisystem collagenopathy and the leading cause of inherited and pediatric rhegmatogenous retinal detachment. This guide provides a deep dive into its genetic heterogeneity, ocular phenotypes, and the life-saving Cambridge Prophylaxis protocol.

sections.title: Clinical Definition & Overview
sections.content: Stickler Syndrome is a group of genetic disorders affecting connective tissue, specifically collagen types II, IX, and XI. It is characterized by a distinctive 'optically empty' vitreous, high myopia, and a high risk of giant retinal tears (GRT). Systemically, it manifests as orofacial abnormalities (Pierre Robin sequence), sensorineural/conductive hearing loss, and premature osteoarthritis.

branches: Type 1: Membranous (Plicated membranes in retrolental space)
Early PVD: Spontaneous and often complete

sections.title: Diagnostic Red Flags (Emergency Signs)
content: Sudden shower of floaters or flashes in a myopic child
Giant Retinal Tear (GRT) > 90 degrees
Stridor or feeding difficulties in neonates (Pierre Robin)
Acute onset of high IOP (Secondary Glaucoma)
Rapidly progressing nuclear sclerotic cataract (presenile)

sections.title: Ocular Examination Findings
content: Refraction: High Myopia (usually > -6.00D), non-progressive
Slit Lamp: Retrolental membranes or beads; cortical/nuclear cataracts
Gonioscopy: Prominent iris processes and angle anomalies in 10%
Fundoscopy: Radial perivascular pigmentary degeneration (RPPD)
Lattice-like degeneration: Often circumferential or atypical
Vitreous: Syneresis and liquefaction

branches: Craniofacial: Flat midface, saddle nose, micrognathia
Palate: Cleft palate, Bifid uvula, Pierre Robin Sequence

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup & Investigations
content: Step 1: Comprehensive dilated fundus exam with scleral depression
Step 2: Expert Slit Lamp biomicroscopy of the vitreous (Goldmann lens)
Step 3: Audiometry (high-frequency SNHL) and Speech/Language evaluation
Step 4: Skeletal surveys (X-rays of hips, spine, and knees)
Step 5: Genetic testing (Multigene panels for COL2A1, COL11A1, COL11A2)
Step 6: Echocardiogram (minor association with MVP)

rows: More severe hearing loss, short stature, thickened skull bones, more pronounced facial features.
Isolated Ocular findings; VCAN gene; NO systemic features; Low risk of RD.
COL18A1; Encephalocele, severe high myopia, vitreoretinal degeneration.
COL2A1; Severe dwarfism, 'dumbbell' shaped long bones, prominent joints.
Severe short-trunk dwarfism, coxa vara, possible RD.

sections.title: Surgical Management: Retinal Detachment
content: 1. Pre-operative stabilization and marking of all breaks
2. Scleral Buckling: Primary choice for simple RRD in kids
3. Pars Plana Vitrectomy (PPV): Often required for Giant Retinal Tears (GRT)
4. Heavy Liquid (PFCL): Crucial for stabilizing the retina during GRT repair
5. Long-acting Tamponade: Silicone oil is frequently preferred due to PVR risk

sections.title: The Cambridge Prophylaxis Protocol
sections.content: The Cambridge Protocol involves 360-degree cryotherapy (or laser) to the ora serrata and vitreous base. Landmark studies by Fincham et al. demonstrated a massive reduction in RD risk: from 73% in untreated eyes to 8% in treated eyes. This is now considered the standard of care for Stickler Type 1 patients.

content.explanation: S: Skeletal (Arthritis/Hypermobility), T: Tongue (Pierre Robin), I: Inherited (AD), C: Cataracts/Cleft Palate, K: Knee/Joint pain, L: Liquefied Vitreous, E: Empty Vitreous, R: Retinal Detachment.

sections.title: Surgical Complications & Challenges
content: Proliferative Vitreoretinopathy (PVR) is highly prevalent (over 50% in some series)
Post-operative glaucoma (steroid-induced or angle-related)
Multiple breaks and posterior extension of lattice
Poor surgical visibility due to early cataracts
Choroidal effusions post-cryotherapy

sections.title: Recent Advances & Landmark Studies
content: Cambridge Prophylaxis Trial: Confirmed 360° cryotherapy reduces RD risk by 10-fold in Type 1 Stickler.
AI Vitreous Analysis: Utilizing deep learning on OCT to differentiate Type 1 vs Type 2 vitreous phenotypes.
Gene Therapy: Early-stage research into COL2A1 mRNA modulation to prevent collagen cross-linking failure.
Ultra-widefield Imaging: Essential for early detection of radial perivascular pigmentary changes in the periphery.

content.explanation: If a child has high myopia and you see NO vitreous structure on slit lamp, it's not a 'good view'—it's Stickler until proven otherwise. Check the palate and ask about joint pain!

sections.title: Prognosis and Follow-up
content: Lifelong 6-12 month follow-up with widefield imaging
Genetic counseling is mandatory (50% risk to offspring)
Visual prognosis is good if RD is prevented/treated early
Hearing aids significantly improve quality of life
Avoid contact sports to minimize trauma-induced RD risk
